THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 09.07.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 BAIL APPL. NO. 7989 OF 2025  2  2025:KER:51502  BECHU KURIAN THOMAS, J.
 -----------------------------------
 B.A.No.7989 of 2025  ------------------------------------
 Dated this the 9th day of July, 2025  ORDER
This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the 2nd accused in Crime No.14 of 2017 of Poonthura Police Station,
Thiruvananthapuram, registered for the offences punishable under sections 294, 323, 420, 417, 506 and 120-B r/w. Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. According to the prosecution, accused 1 to 3 promised to arrange a foreign visa to the defacto complainant and collected an amount of Rs.25,000/- from him, thereafter failed to arrange the Visa or return the amount and thereby committed the offences alleged.
4.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that petitioner is the wife of the first accused and she has no involvement in the crime alleged.

It was further submitted that the FIR was registered as early as in 2017 and BAIL APPL. NO. 7989 OF 2025 2025:KER:51502 now the petitioner is being proposed to be arrested and therefore she ought to be protected with an order of pre-arrest bail.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand submitted that the prosecution allegations are serious and therefore custodial interrogation is essential.

It was also submitted that initially the investigation was closed referring the case as 'undetected' and subsequently further investigation was ordered and the District Crime Branch has taken over the investigation.
7. On a consideration of the contentions, it is noticed that the crime was registered on 01.01.2017 alleging offences committed by the petitioner and also her husband who is the first accused.

Though there are allegations that the accused had promised a Visa to be arranged to the defacto complainant, since the petitioner alleges that the entire transactions were carried out by her Nisa vs State Of Kerala on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15822269/
2 husband-the first accused and she had no role at all other than being present when the defacto complainant came to visit him, I am of the view that custodial interrogation can be avoided especially since the petitioner is a lady.

8. In Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another [(2020) 5 SCC 1], it was held that while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail or not, Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the BAIL APPL. NO. 7989 OF 2025 2025:KER:51502 applicant, and the facts of the case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another [(2020) 5 SCC 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Grant of anticipatory bail is a matter of discretion and the kind of conditions to be imposed or not to be imposed are all dependent on facts of each case, and subject to the discretion of the court.

9. In Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274], it has been held that a mere assertion on the part of the State while opposing the plea for anticipatory bail that custodial interrogation is required would not be sufficient and that the State would have to show or indicate more than prima facie case as to why custodial interrogation of the accused is required for the purpose of investigation.

entities.text: Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the State has not been able to convince this Court that custodial interrogation is necessary.

10. Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 18.07.2025 and shall subject herself to interrogation.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioner, then, she shall be released on bail on her executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the BAIL APPL. NO. 7989 OF 2025 2025:KER:51502 witnesses; nor shall she tamper with the evidence.
(e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while she is on bail.
(f) Petitioner shall not leave India without the permission of the Court having jurisdiction.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.
